label: Early original-phase input of 1/x/m/n/f/0/z/j after a prefix dominated by z/f/o/j/1/x/0/3/t/m/c
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, almost entirely at positions 2-6 (peak at t=3; none at t=0, at the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase). The current input is nearly always one of a small token set: 1 is by far the strongest (54% of mass, 14x lift), then x, m, n, f, 0, z, j; it essentially never fires on other tokens. Whether it fires, and how strongly, depends on the preceding context: it is strongest when all or nearly all earlier inputs come from a second set (z, f, o, j, 1, x, 0, 3, t, m, c). Top examples look like "3 t f z [1]" and "c f z [1]", while "k i [1]" with unrelated prefix tokens does not fire. It is also more active when the sequence has more digits. The behaviour looks like a graded, roughly additive function of the prefix tokens rather than a crisp rule: the best predicate (current token in set A, at most one earlier input outside set B, t<=6) reaches only dev F1 ~0.55 and mass recall ~0.71. Many misses are weak activations on 1 after unrelated prefixes, and many false positives are A-tokens that do not fire.
